flags: Visit Maryland gives Hollywood–Edgemere, 106 miles and 3–4 hours; the byways encyclopedia gives Solomons–Baltimore, while material maps 136.6 miles. Used tourism’s itinerary scope and length; route geometry needs reconciliation.

Material’s strip miles restart on a second segment. Driving sequence follows the cached tourism itinerary: Sotterley, Solomons, St. Leonard, Benedict, Upper Marlboro, Bladensburg, Baltimore, North Point/Edgemere.
No construction or designation-campaign history is supplied for the modern byway. Overview explains the commemorated campaign without claiming modern roads duplicate the exact 1814 troop route.
Visit Maryland contains an erroneous March 1812 landing caption; its main narrative places the campaign in 1814. Used August 18, 1814 from the Benedict article.

Tourism says a large flag was visible at dawn but does not describe the flag change. Fort McHenry article explicitly distinguishes the storm flag from the garrison flag; material’s claim that the large flag still flew at dawn is not reused.

Sotterley acreage differs between tourism (100) and encyclopedia (95); omitted acreage. Enslaved people’s names, escape history and present descendant participation follow tourism; no descendant-authored source is cached.
Modern byway-building history remains absent. Aquasco’s documented early road network supplies local road history without equating those roads with the entire scenic corridor.
